messages:
Marta - Procurement: Morning — VectorPulse sent a renewal with a weird commit ladder and a conversion multiplier for high-dim vectors. Can team triage cost/risk? Proposal in Drive: https://drive.google.com/vectorpulse-quote. @Linh @Omar @Kavi @Zoe

Linh (Finance): Please paste the pricing lines here. We should compare 12-month TCO under base and growth scenarios.

Marta - Procurement: Quote excerpt:

```
Option A - Throughput Commit:
  Level 1: 250M embeddings/mo @ $0.000014/embed
  Level 2: 500M embeddings/mo @ $0.000012/embed
  Level 3: 1.0B embeddings/mo @ $0.000010/embed
  Annual true-up at quarter end
Addendum: For vectors >1024 dims apply a 1.4x conversion multiplier
Option B - Seat-like Throughput Units:
  5 TPUs @ $1,600/mo each = $8,000/mo
  Each TPU includes 60M embeddings/mo pooled
  Overage: $0.000009/embed
  Ingestion/one-time import fee: $5,000 for >2M vectors
```

Omar (ML Eng): Conversion multiplier is a blocker. Our personalization models use 1536-dim vectors; that would upsell our volume by 1.4x which changes economics materially. If multiplier is enforced per-dim, committed tiers become less attractive.

Kavi (Platform): Also need to confirm metering: do they count batched calls as N vectors or N API calls? Do partial failures get retried and counted twice? We need meter-spec clarity before committing.

VectorPulse Rep: Hi all ":wave:" — thanks for the read. Multiplier applies only for batch-imported high-dim vectors that exceed 1M vectors/month; normal streaming calls are metered 1:1 regardless of dim. We can make exceptions for enterprise customers. Metering is per-embedding vector processed (batched calls count by vector count). Partial retries are excluded when they can be proven in logs.

Linh (Finance): If multiplier stays for our use-case we should model it. Quick calc: current ~110M/mo @1536d. With 1.4x multiplier that's billed as 154M/mo. Option A at level 1 => 154M * 0.000014 = $2,156/mo (~$25.9k/yr). Option B fixed = $8k/mo. Looks like Level pricing could be cheapest if discount at Level 2/3 applies as we grow. But ingestion fee + multiplier could flip the choice.

Omar (ML Eng): Engineering asks: can VectorPulse provide a sample bill for April (our peak import month) showing the conversion math and a peak-month scenario with TPU vs throughput commit? Need to validate their meter logs against our telemetry.

Zoe (Legal): Contract asks: remove unilateral conversion multiplier or define clear thresholds and audit right. Add dispute process and timeline for billing disagreements. Also need data export/retention and termination wind-down language.

VectorPulse Rep: Understood. We can: (1) remove multiplier for customers who sign a 12mo commit at Level 2 or above, (2) provide a CSV sample invoice with line-itemized charges (reserved vs overage vs ingestion), and (3) supply meter logs for a 30-day lookback for audit. We'll draft amended terms for the multiplier and dispute process.

Marta - Procurement: Good. Please send the revised quote with two firm options: one with multiplier removed (Level 2 commit) and one with multiplier but lower per-embed price. Also include sample invoice for a peak import month and the meter-spec doc.

VectorPulse Rep: Will send revised quote + sample invoice + meter-spec by EOD tomorrow. Also confirm US-West and EU-West residency and daily billing export on enterprise plan.

Kavi (Platform): Ask them to include per-team invoice breakdowns (line items per project tag) and a billing API or S3 export for ingestion details.

Linh (Finance): Also request an annual price cap (max 7%) and optional monthly true-up vs quarterly to match our forecasting cadence.

Marta - Procurement: @Procurement-Bot open PR when docs arrive. Approvers: Linh (Finance), Zoe (Legal), Security.

Procurement-Bot: Created PR #536: "VectorPulse renewal + conversion multiplier review". Approvers requested: Linh (Finance), Zoe (Legal), Security. Link: https://procurement.internal/pr/536

Marta - Procurement: Thanks everyone. Once revised quote lands well run a 20-min cost-impact review and decide path. :thumbsup:
